items.followUp: Define metals and non-metals, and give one characteristic of each.

rubric.why: Tests the defining electron-transfer tendency of metals.
rubric.description: Defines metals as elements that tend to lose electrons and form positive ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both losing electrons and forming positive ions.

rubric.why: Tests the defining electron behaviour of non-metals.
rubric.description: Defines non-metals as elements that tend to gain electrons to form negative ions or share electrons in covalent compounds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either accepted description.

modelAnswer: Metals are elements that tend to lose electrons and form positive ions.
Non-metals are elements that tend to gain electrons to form negative ions, or share electrons to form covalent bonds.

items.followUp: Write the balanced equation for the reaction of chlorine with hot concentrated NaOH solution.

rubric.why: The question assesses the products and balanced equation for chlorine with cold, dilute sodium hydroxide.
rubric.description: Gives the balanced reaction: Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H₂O.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct products and 1 mark for the correctly balanced equation.

modelAnswer: Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaClO + H₂O

items.followUp: An atom has mass number A = 235 and atomic number Z = 92. Find its number of protons and neutrons.

rubric.why: The atomic number gives the number of protons.
rubric.description: States that the atom has 92 protons.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct number of protons.

rubric.why: Neutron number is the mass number minus the atomic number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using A − Z and 1 mark for the correct neutron number.

modelAnswer: Given: A = 238, Z = 92.
Number of protons = Z = 92.
Number of neutrons = A − Z.
Number of neutrons = 238 − 92 = 146.
The atom has 92 protons and 146 neutrons.

items.followUp: Define bonding electrons and explain how a double bond forms in an oxygen molecule, O₂.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of bonding electrons.
rubric.description: Defines bonding electrons as electrons shared between atoms to form a covalent bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the shared electrons or electron pair involved in bonding.

rubric.why: Checks the electron-sharing explanation and bond count in methane.
rubric.description: Explains that carbon shares one electron with each of four hydrogen atoms, forming four single covalent bonds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for sharing with four hydrogen atoms and 1 mark for stating that four single covalent bonds form.

rubric.why: Checks the bonding arrangement in acetylene.
rubric.description: Explains that the two carbon atoms share three pairs of electrons, forming a triple bond, and each carbon forms a single bond with one hydrogen atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the carbon–carbon triple bond and 1 mark for the carbon–hydrogen single bonds.

modelAnswer: Bonding electrons are the electrons shared between atoms to form a covalent bond.
In CH₄, carbon shares one electron with each of four hydrogen atoms.
This sharing forms four single covalent bonds:
H
H—C—H
H
In C₂H₂, each carbon shares three pairs of electrons with the other carbon, forming a triple bond.
Each carbon also forms a single bond with one hydrogen atom: H—C≡C—H.

items.followUp: Explain how an increase in temperature and wind speed affects the rate of evaporation.

rubric.why: Temperature is one factor affecting evaporation; the answer should state its effect.
rubric.description: States that higher temperature increases the rate of evaporation, because particles have more kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming temperature and 1 mark for its effect or explanation.

rubric.why: A second factor is required, with its effect on evaporation.
rubric.description: Gives another factor affecting evaporation, such as surface area, wind speed or humidity, and states its effect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a valid second factor and 1 mark for the correct effect or explanation.

modelAnswer: Two factors affecting evaporation are temperature and surface area.
A higher temperature gives particles more kinetic energy, so more particles escape from the liquid and evaporation becomes faster.
A larger surface area exposes more particles to the air, so evaporation becomes faster.

items.followUp: What is a radical? Give one example of a positive radical.

rubric.why: Checks the defining structure and charge of a radical.
rubric.description: Defines a radical as an atom or group of atoms carrying a positive or negative charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying an atom or group of atoms with a charge.

rubric.why: Checks that the student can give a valid example of a radical.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example, such as sulfate, ammonium, hydroxide or nitrate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any correct radical and its formula.

modelAnswer: A radical is an atom or group of atoms carrying a positive or negative charge and behaving as a single unit in a chemical reaction.
Example: sulfate ion, SO₄²⁻.

items.followUp: Define formula unit and give the formula unit of magnesium oxide.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of a formula unit in an ionic compound.
rubric.description: Defines a formula unit as the simplest whole-number ratio of ions in an ionic compound.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the simplest whole-number ratio of ions.

rubric.why: Checks understanding through a correct example.
rubric.description: Gives a correct ionic example and its constituent ions, such as NaCl (Na⁺ and Cl⁻) or MgO (Mg²⁺ and O²⁻).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example with the appropriate ions.

modelAnswer: A formula unit is the simplest whole-number ratio of ions in an ionic compound.
For example, the formula unit NaCl represents a 1:1 ratio of Na⁺ ions to Cl⁻ ions.

items.followUp: The empirical formula of a compound is CH₂ and its molecular mass is 42. Find its molecular formula.

rubric.why: Checks the relationship used to derive a molecular formula from an empirical formula.
rubric.description: States that the molecular formula is the empirical formula multiplied by n, where n = molecular mass ÷ empirical formula mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relationship and value of n.

rubric.why: Checks application of the relationship to a valid example.
rubric.description: Uses CH₂O with empirical formula mass 30 and molecular mass 180 to find n = 6, giving C₆H₁₂O₆.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct worked example and molecular formula.

modelAnswer: Molecular formula = (empirical formula)ₙ, where n = molecular mass ÷ empirical formula mass.
For glucose, the empirical formula is CH₂O and its empirical formula mass is 12 + (2 × 1) + 16 = 30.
Molecular formula = (CH₂O)₆ = C₆H₁₂O₆.
